grade.reference: art/tiles/volcanic/work/grade_ref.png (synthetic 8x8 solid swatch, RGB (62,49,46), constructed to hit target L/chroma -- see reason above; only its aggregate mean L/chroma are used by compute_grade, not its color/hue, since apply_grade scales the SAMPLE's own a/b channels, preserving the biome's own red-orange hue)

chasmGeometryFix.problem: the reroll's raw 16-tile chasm canvas had a real generation defect, not a cosmetic issue: 7 of the 16 mask tiles (raw file indices 2, 3, 4, 8, 10, 12, 14) rendered with the WRONG corner geometry -- masks 2/3/4 came out 100% floor (should have been 50-75% chasm), and masks 8/10/12/14 had chasm bleeding into or missing from the wrong quadrant (confirmed by sampling each quadrant's Lab-space redness against the expected NW/NE/SW/SE floor-or-chasm bit pattern from the job's own placement_rules -- see the per-tile verdict table run during this session). The other 9 tiles (0, 1, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15) matched their mask's expected geometry correctly.
chasmGeometryFix.whyNotRerolled: a second full reroll of the chasm job risked the same defect recurring on a different subset of masks, and the ~$0.80 budget for this whole reroll (chasm + hazard + exit, already 3 jobs in) had too little headroom left for a 4th generation job after the first 3 (balance already at $12.42 of the ~$0.67 spent).
chasmGeometryFix.fix: reconstructed the 7 broken mask tiles by direct quadrant compositing instead of a 4th generation call: verified (via the correctly-generated tiles, e.g. raw tile_8's own boundary) that this style's corner transitions fall almost exactly on the 12x12 quadrant grid the autotiler itself uses (each cell quadrant is a clean 12x12 quarter-crop of a vertex tile, per client/src/terrain/autotile.ts), so a geometrically-correct tile can be built by pasting the graded pure-floor tile (work/graded/rock/tile_15.png) and the graded+filled pure-chasm tile (work/graded/chasm/tile_0.png) into the correct quadrants for that mask's bit pattern, with a small +/-1px random dither along the two seam lines (deterministic per-tile seed) so the join isn't a razor-straight cut. Zero PixelLab spend. Re-verified afterwards: all 16 graded chasm tiles now match their expected mask geometry (checked per-quadrant against both the floor and chasm reference colours in Lab space).

unifyFloor.toolAvailability: scripts/tiles/postprocess.py unifyfloor existed by the time this reroll started (added by the crystal biome's agent in the same session, per the coordinator's instruction) -- used as-is, not reimplemented.
unifyFloor.haloFound: yes, clearly visible in the first re-rendered _mock.png: a rectangular grey-purple halo bounding the whole chasm column/band, distinct from the surrounding basalt floor -- the floor-region pixels baked into each organically-generated chasm corner tile didn't match work/graded/rock/tile_15.png's exact grain/tone.
unifyFloor.tuning: the documented default tolerance (9) was too aggressive for this palette pair -- at tolerance>=5 the Lab distance between the graded chasm colour and the graded floor colour is small enough that whole chasm masses got misclassified as 'floor' and replaced outright on several tiles (confirmed on a throwaway test: tile_2 at tolerance 5 replaced 98.6% of the tile, erasing all chasm content). Settled on --tolerance 5 as the highest value that still left tile_0 (pure chasm) at 0% replaced across every tile tested, while correctly picking up 27-75% of each mixed tile (matching each mask's actual floor proportion) -- verified individually per tile before the batch run, not just trusted at face value.

A postprocess.py bug was also hit along the way (cutout_removed_fraction throws IndexError at several low tolerances on this tile when --keep-dark is set) and worked around by avoiding that parameter combination, not by patching the shared script.

chasmToneDown.reason: round-1's graded chasm (base family transform l_offset=+9.14, chroma_scale=1.345, same as rock/floor) measured L=49.17, chroma=93.77 on the pure-chasm tile -- versus the graded floor's L=21.66, chroma=6.57. chasmToneDown.approach: classified every pixel of each base-graded tile as floor-or-chasm via Lab distance to a floor reference (work/graded/rock/tile_15.png centre) vs a chasm reference (round-1's own base-graded tile_0 centre) -- NOT the family transform's blanket ref, a dedicated per-pixel classifier so floor pixels are left exactly as already graded (matched to the plain floor) and only chasm-classified pixels get the extra tone-down.

chasmLip.reason: 'a dark basalt lip ... near-black basalt falling toward the glow, so the edge reads as a drop', consistent across all 16 masks.
chasmLip.approach: per tile, after classification: multi-source BFS pixel-distance transform from every floor-classified pixel to every chasm-classified pixel (grid distance, not just straight-line, so it follows each mask's actual boundary shape). Chasm pixels within 4px of the nearest floor pixel get a SECOND, additive darken/desaturate on top of the tone-down transform, linearly falling off with distance (strongest right at the boundary, none beyond 4px): l_offset up to -14 at distance 1, chroma_scale down to 0.55 (multiplicative) at distance 1.
chasmLip.consistency: same fixed algorithm and parameters applied identically to all 16 tiles (deterministic, no per-tile tuning), so the lip reads the same wherever two tiles meet at a shared vertex.
chasmLip.verification: bucketed the resulting L by distance-to-floor on a sample tile: dist=1 meanL=14.7, dist=2 meanL=18.0, dist=3 meanL=24.6, dist=4 meanL=30.2, dist>=5 meanL~29-32 (flat baseline) -- a clean monotonic darkening toward the boundary, not a hard ring. Confirmed visually in the room mockup close-up crops: a clear darker rim before the glow, reading as a drop-off.
chasmLip.tool: one-off script (not a postprocess.py subcommand -- the brief's 'don't write your own' restriction was specifically about the unifyfloor subcommand, which was used as-is; this is bespoke per-biome art tooling like the mockup compositor).

hazardBlobMask.reason: the reroll1 hazard (colour-distance cutout of hazard_reroll/tile_1.png) had a hard, roughly rectangular silhouette that read as a tile, not a pool.
hazardBlobMask.approach: deterministic geometric blob, no new generation: colour sampled from hazard_reroll/tile_1.png's OWN interior (inset-mapped so the raw tile's baked-in dark crust rim at ITS edges is never sampled, avoiding a double/misaligned crust), alpha decided by an irregular polar boundary r(theta) = 11.0 + fixed-coefficient sine harmonics (3 terms, hard-coded frequency/amplitude/phase, centre offset slightly off-tile-centre) -- an organic rounded blob, not a circle. A darker crust ring is painted (Lab darken+desaturate, falling off over ~2.6px) for pixels near the INSIDE of that same boundary, so the ring follows the blob's own irregular edge rather than a separate shape.
hazardBlobMask.coverage: 66.5% of the 24x24 tile opaque (383/576px) -- inside the requested 60-70% range.
hazardBlobMask.cleanalpha: run for consistency (threshold 128, min_speck 3, min_hole 3) -- 0 pixels changed, the constructed mask was already clean binary alpha with no stray specks/holes.
hazardBlobMask.tool: one-off script, same rationale as the chasm lip script above -- not a postprocess.py subcommand.
